limitations: One row, two workers, compressed time and attempt budget. Downstream idempotent billing effects and legacy queue adoption are separate obligations.
The model permits overlapping handlers after lease expiry. Settlement checks token ownership exactly as the repository does.

Finite verification domain. One row, two workers, four distinct lease tokens, time 0..6, retry budget 3. Values beyond these bounds are outside this instance; generation and revision values never wrap.

The model assumes the private namespace routes to the correct organization/day owner. The operator must supply a complete, genuinely quiesced snapshot. The object validates the asserted flag, key shape, and values.

Caller authorization, positive scaled amount and limits, exact day rollover, key encoding and multiple organizations are outside the finite model. The Workerd suite checks rollover, cross-organization behavior and rejection when metering is missing.

Live reserve and release have no operation identity. A repeated call after an ambiguous reply can apply a second mutation. Release clamps the counters independently and does not prove aggregate conservation or single settlement.

The model abstracts a SQL transaction as atomic with a single clock sample. It serializes post-commit schedule and reply phases. It does not prove provider usage settlement, storage availability, precise Cloudflare alarm retries, or a delivery deadline.
One provider phase, two workers, three attempts. Whole-account phase ordering, cancellation, export, database erasure and billing-specific completion guards require separate models.
Provider idempotency is abstracted as a monotone applied flag. Adapter inspection is assumed authoritative.

Finite verification domain. One provider phase, two workers, four lease generations, attempt budget 3, time 0..6. Values beyond these bounds are outside this instance; generation and revision values never wrap.
Models coordinator phase/publication ordering. Claim/lease repository CAS, exact attestation crypto, per-await rollback recovery and node/provider lifecycle are separate unmodeled obligations.
Failure before runtime impact is retryable; post-impact pre-publication failure is represented by completed rollback. Rollback-in-progress failures need a separate model.

Finite verification domain. One operation and previous/candidate runtime, all explicit coordinator phases, abstract atomic publication and rollback. Values beyond these bounds are outside this instance; generation and revision values never wrap.
